label: Measured classification of all 713 current verify mismatches: 574 (80.5%) are era drift (stored X.Y differs from the current skill anchor), 134 (18.8%) W-only build drift, 5 other; 8 files carry a stale nonzero Z. The era segment, not the git-derived W, is the dominant stale component.

No in-repo consumer reads a child document's stored version: the gate checks presence/format only, the validators require version on skills (SKILL.md), and the only equality consumer is verify, which has no caller.

The per-doc field's stated value is an era stamp inherited from the owning skill's anchor; inside the skill tree that era is already known from SKILL.md and changelog, so the field is a restatement, and the standard already documents that nothing keeps duplicated hub versions in parity.
Two of the four segments assert nothing durable per doc: Z is a reserved placeholder seeded 0 with no producer or consumer, and W is git history that no consumer can reproduce without the repository.

The field's cost is structural: anchor bumps stale X.Y on every child doc, content commits stale W, convergence needs per-doc discipline, and no automated surface reconciles equality; measured today as 574 era-drift flags under an enforcement-active rollout that covers presence and format only.

Q4 answer: the per-doc version should not exist as an asserted per-doc invariant. Keep version on SKILL.md as the anchor of record; remove it from child doc classes, or at most retain an era-only child stamp. The reversal criterion is a defined requirement for per-doc era identification outside the skill tree; none is defined in-repo.
No in-repo consumer of a child doc's version exists; its only enforced assertions are presence and four-part format.
Measured 2026-10-11: sk-code 332 mismatches (306 era, 23 W-only, 3 other, 3 Z-residue); sk-doc 266 (153 era, 111 W-only, 2 other, 3 Z-residue); system-skill-advisor 115 (115 era, 2 Z-residue).
